content: 1. Tipranavir Dosing Recommendations: For patients weighing less than 36 kg, tipranavir is not recommended due to the lack of a suitable formulation. For patients weighing 36 kg or more, the recommended dose is 500 mg orally every 12 hours, co-administered with ritonavir 200 mg orally every 12 hours (boosted therapy). Ritonavir is essential to achieve proper dosing and adequate blood levels. Dose adjustments are not necessary for mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A). However, concurrent use is contraindicated in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class B or C). 2. Indications: Tipranavir is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-experienced patients infected with HIV-1 strains resistant to multiple protease inhibitors. It must be used with ritonavir and other antiretroviral agents. 3. Pediatric Use: Safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 2 years of age. For children aged 2 years or older and weighing less than 36 kg, tipranavir is not recommended due to the lack of a suitable pediatric formulation. For children aged 2 years or older and weighing 36 kg or more, the dose is 14 mg/kg plus ritonavir 6 mg/kg orally every 12 hours, or 375 mg/m² plus ritonavir 150 mg/m² orally every 12 hours. The dose should not exceed the adult dose of 500 mg plus ritonavir 200 mg orally every 12 hours. 4. Drug Interactions: Contraindicated Medications: Tipranavir significantly increases the levels of certain drugs by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4, leading to potential toxicity. These drugs include: Alfuzosin, alprazolam, amiodarone, aprepitant, atorvastatin, cobicistat, cobimetinib, conivaptan, dihydroergotamine (including intranasal forms), elbasvir/grazoprevir, eletriptan, eliglustat, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, enzalutamide, eplerenone, ergoloid mesylates, ergotamine, isavuconazonium sulfate, ivabradine, lomitapide, lonafarnib, lovastatin, lurasidone, mavacamten, methylprednisolone, naloxegol, nelfinavir, pacritinib, pimozide, propafenone, quinidine, regorafenib, rifampin, simvastatin, St. John’s Wort, triazolam, venetoclax, and voclosporin. Drugs Requiring Dose Adjustments or Monitoring: Tipranavir may increase or decrease the levels of certain drugs, necessitating dose adjustments or close monitoring. Examples include: Acalabrutinib, ado-trastuzumab emtansine, afatinib, apalutamide, aripiprazole, atazanavir, axitinib, bedaquiline, bosentan, bosutinib, brigatinib, bromocriptine, cabergoline, cabozantinib, carbamazepine, ceritinib, cimetidine, clarithromycin, copanlisib, cyclosporine, dabigatran, dabrafenib, daridorexant, dasatinib, diazepam, disopyramide, dolutegravir, doxorubicin (including liposomal forms), dronedarone, duloxetine, edoxaban, encorafenib, entrectinib, erdafitinib, erythromycin (various forms), ethinyloestradiol, everolimus, fedratinib, fentanyl (all forms), and others. Hormonal Contraceptives: Tipranavir may alter estrogen plasma levels, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 5. Special Considerations: Hepatic Impairment: Tipranavir is contraindicated in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment due to the risk of toxicity. Drug Manufacturing Interference: Tipranavir may interfere with the manufacturing of certain cell-based therapies, such as atidarsagene autotemcel and betibeglogene autotemcel. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization or apheresis procedures. 6. Monitoring and Adjustments: For drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, co-administration with tipranavir often requires dose reductions or alternative therapies to avoid toxicity. 7. Warnings: Co-administration of tipranavir with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers can lead to significant changes in drug levels, resulting in either toxicity or reduced efficacy. Tipranavir capsules contain alcohol, which may cause disulfiram-like reactions when used with disulfiram or metronidazole.
